decision.reverted: 1da32a5 capture handoff, reverted by b0319c1 after neither valid comparison demonstrated a stable gain

notes: Bridge 5 activation is verified via live GNOME RPC, not inferred from installed files. Both arms of this formal comparison use bridge 5; it does not independently isolate bridge 4 versus 5.
Do not subtract the prior 131.056 ms to claim a code gain: network RTT, user workload, desktop session and Mac content size changed after reboot.
No concurrent compilation, profiler or test gates during formal samples; no round or spike was discarded.

Before sampling ping averaged 6.421 ms; after sampling one ping took 121.087 ms and the four-packet average was 35.362 ms. The network has substantial outliers; this does not identify the cause of each slow input.
Separate Cargo target directories and distinct binary hashes were verified before sampling. An initial shared-target build reused one cached binary and was rejected before any test run.
Formal Linux internal timestamps and first response readback/I420 IDs are unavailable and remain null. Diagnostics supply separate complete correlations.

Per-stage percentiles are independent and cannot be added. The mixed residual is (Mac received - Mac write end) minus (Linux final write end - Agent received); it is not pure or one-way network latency.
H.264 codec pad timing is distinct from the whole encode call, which includes input padding and color conversion.

The capture-handoff candidate was reverted after both valid comparisons had a higher candidate P95 and no median gain; this observation does not prove the cause of each outlier. Production Agent and network binaries stayed unchanged, and GNOME bridge 5 remains active. WebRTC is absent.
The invalid repeat is retained in full and excluded only because the predeclared Mac geometry condition failed; no slow input was removed from valid rounds.
The first final Linux unit archive lacked two included Python fixtures; this compile failure is retained and the complete archived test files were added before the successful rerun.
